To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cueing communicatives intentions may facilitate the comprehension of implied interpretations and that this facilitation may be immediate.

(i) cueing communicative intent affects language processing, (ii) cueing may affect language processing already at an early level of language comprehension (iii) the way of cue-ing communicative intent affects processing, and (iv) cueing communicatve intent may be more effective when the cueing is unambiguous by matching the pragmatic conventions of the language.

(1) the use of quotation marks is effective for the immediate comprehension of ironic language, (2) the effectiveness of quotation marks depends on their pragmatic convention, (3) pragmatic reanalysis may be immediately triggered by the use of quotation, and (4) the comprehension of irony requires additional information, which is provided in our study by the use of the quotation mark.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the way of how communicative intentions are conveyed in digital communication, and how this affects the way of how utterances are processed.
the way in which pragmatic information can be used to convey communicative intent in digital communication.
pragmatic aspects of language comprehension in the digital era.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cueing communicatives intentions is a very important and effective tool for the comprehension of irony, but only in the case of unambiguous cues.
cueing of communicative intentions is effective in the sense that it allows for an immediate reanalysis of utterances in order to understand them as intended.

the ERP results indicate that the processing of ironic language is affected by the cueing of the speaker’s communicative intention, but that the effect depends on the cueing method and the pragmatic conventions of the cueing method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain is able to process the intended communicative meaning of utterances, even when the speaker is not present.
ERP evidence from cueing communicative intent is crucial for understanding language in the digital world.
ERP evidence for the immediate effect of cues for communicative intentions can be obtained by means of quotation mark cues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ERP research may help to understand how communicative intentions are conveyed in digital communication.
pragmatic conventions may play a crucial role in digital communication, and that they may be exploited to improve the comprehension of irony in online communication.
the way of cue usage may affect language processing, and that pragmatic cues may be used for communicative intentions, even in absence of a face-to-face interaction.
